question: Can invalid reasoning demonstrations, shown alongside valid ones, improve few-shot chain-of-thought prompting?
hypothesis: Providing both valid and invalid reasoning demonstrations lets the model learn which mistakes to avoid and so improves reasoning over conventional CoT.
contributions: Analyse various invalid reasoning types and find that combining positive and negative demonstrations generally boosts chain-of-thought.
Propose contrastive chain of thought with an automatic method to construct contrastive demonstrations.
Evaluations on multiple reasoning benchmarks show significant improvements over conventional chain of thought.

method.summary: Each few-shot demonstration is extended with a wrong explanation built automatically by extracting object spans (numbers, equations, persons) from the correct rationale with a spaCy entity recognition model and randomly shuffling their positions (incoherent objects). Evaluated on GPT-3.5-Turbo with 4-shot prompts, with and without self-consistency.
method.task: arithmetic reasoning and factual QA via few-shot prompting

models.name: spaCy en_core_web_trf
models.architecture: entity recognition model used to extract object spans

inference.prompting: 4-shot; demonstrations are (Q, T+, A+, T-, A-); simplified CoT format with 'Question:', 'Explanation:', 'Wrong Explanation:' fields (Fig 1); positive rationales taken from Wei et al. 2022b and Wang et al. 2023

parameters.negative_construction: Incoherent Objects: shuffle positions of spaCy-extracted object spans within the correct rationale

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: not defined in the paper; presumably exact final-answer match

eval.protocol: Single run per cell, no seeds, variance or significance test stated; test sets randomly subsampled to at most 500.

prompts.text:
Question: James writes a 3-page letter to 2 different friends twice a week. How many pages does he write a year?
Explanation: He writes each friend 3*2=6 pages a week. So he writes 6*2=12 pages every week. That means he writes 12*52=624 pages a year.
Wrong Explanation: He writes each friend 12*52=624 pages a week. So he writes 3*2=6 pages every week. That means he writes 6*2=12 pages a year.

results.claim: Authors claim every invalid-rationale category helps over plain CoT, contradicting the earlier finding that invalid demos have minimal effect
results.quote: we observe significant gains across all invalid rationale categories compared to conventional chain-of-thought

limits: Only GPT-3.5-Turbo (0301) is tested; no other models or sizes.
No temperature, decoding, number of self-consistency samples, seeds or significance tests are reported, and accuracy is not defined.
Test sets are subsampled to at most 500 items; Bamboogle has 125 and AQuA 254, so differences are noisy.
No ablation of the automatic negative construction against other invalid categories at scale; Table 1 uses manual negatives with differing numbers from Table 2.
No analysis of why contrastive demos help; the claimed reduction in reasoning errors is stated but no number is given.
Few-shot setting only; zero-shot CoT is excluded (footnote 2).
Code described as to be released.
